summary: Mechanical engineering PhD candidate at Northwestern with experience in computational mechanics, topology optimization, and Python-driven simulation pipelines.

bullets.text: Built a multi-material topology optimization pipeline in Python and JAX for soft robotic gel-elastomer composites; co-authored ASME IDETC 2026 submission GELATO.
Wrote finite-element solvers in NumPy and SciPy that reduced per-iteration solve time from 12 to 3 seconds via sparse linear-algebra refactoring.
Trained surrogate models in PyTorch on simulation outputs to accelerate design-space exploration by 40x.
Mentored two junior students on JAX, automatic differentiation, and gradient-based optimization workflows.
Implemented uncertainty quantification routines for material-property estimation in additive manufacturing.
Profiled and optimized a Fortran finite-element kernel; documented results in an internal technical memo.
Presented findings at the lab's summer symposium to a 30-person audience of staff scientists.
Coursework: continuum mechanics, finite elements, computational design optimization, statistical learning.

projects.name: GELATO
projects.description: Open-source topology-optimization library for hydrogel composites.

bullets.text: Designed a JAX-based forward solver supporting heterogeneous element materials and gradient-based design updates.
Built a Streamlit demo for interactive parameter sweeps; used by three collaborating labs.

projects.name: PIANO Eval Harness
projects.description: Personal project: evaluation pipeline for physics-informed neural networks.

bullets.text: Implemented a regression test suite with PyTorch and pytest covering five PINN architectures and four PDE benchmarks.
Containerized the harness with Docker and continuous integration via GitHub Actions.
